item.title: How I generate an Open Graph image for every post
item.content:encoded: How I generate a unique Open Graph preview image for every blog post at build time in Astro, using astro-og-canvas, instead of one shared image.

item.title: New: 90 free tools for developers
item.content:encoded: I launched a new tools section on the site: 90 free calculators and utilities for developers, running entirely in your browser. No signup, no ads.

item.title: How I added search to my static site with Pagefind
item.content:encoded: How I added fast client-side search to my static Astro blog with Pagefind, which indexes your HTML at build time and runs entirely in the browser.

item.title: How to rebuild a Cloudflare site on a schedule
item.content:encoded: Learn how to rebuild a Cloudflare Pages site on a schedule using a deploy hook, triggered either by a GitHub Action cron or a Cloudflare Worker cron.

item.title: Cloudflare Email Workers: run code when an email arrives
item.content:encoded: How to receive and process incoming email with Cloudflare Email Workers, parse it with postal-mime, and forward or act on it.

item.title: Cloudflare Turnstile: stop bots without annoying CAPTCHAs
item.content:encoded: How to protect a form from bots with Cloudflare Turnstile. Add the widget to your page and verify the token from a Worker.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers: secrets and environments
item.content:encoded: How to handle config, secrets, and multiple environments (staging, production) in Cloudflare Workers without leaking anything.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers observability: logs and traces
item.content:encoded: Learn how to see what your Cloudflare Worker does in production using console.log, observability in wrangler.jsonc, and live tailing with wrangler tail.

item.title: Cloudflare Analytics Engine: store and query metrics
item.content:encoded: How to write custom events from a Worker with Analytics Engine and query them later with SQL. Cheap, high-volume time-series data.

item.title: The AI Workshop (July 2026 cohort)
item.content:encoded: The AI Workshop July 2026 cohort covers agents, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, MCP, skills, subagents, and practical AI workflows.

item.title: Cloudflare Cron Triggers: run a Worker on a schedule
item.content:encoded: How to run a Cloudflare Worker on a schedule with Cron Triggers. Nightly jobs, periodic checks, and cleanups, with no server to keep running.

item.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects: state that lives in one place
item.content:encoded: What Durable Objects are and how to use them, with their built-in SQLite storage. A simple counter and a rate limiter, explained from scratch.

item.title: Cloudflare Queues: run work in the background
item.content:encoded: How to use Cloudflare Queues to do work after the response is sent. Producers, consumers, batching, retries, and dead letter queues.

item.title: Cloudflare R2: object storage without egress fees
item.content:encoded: How to store and serve files like images and uploads with Cloudflare R2 from a Worker. S3-compatible storage with no egress fees.

item.title: Cloudflare KV: a key-value store for your Workers
item.content:encoded: Learn how to use Cloudflare Workers KV, an edge key-value store, to create a namespace and put and get data, ideal for sessions, feature flags and caching.

item.title: Cloudflare D1: a SQL database for your Workers
item.content:encoded: How to create a D1 database, manage its schema with migrations, and query it from a Worker. SQLite, served from the edge.

item.title: Serving a website with Cloudflare Workers static assets
item.content:encoded: How to deploy a static site, an SPA, or a full Astro app on Cloudflare Workers using the static assets feature, with a Worker for the dynamic parts.

item.title: Wrangler: the Cloudflare Workers command line tool
item.content:encoded: A practical guide to Wrangler, the CLI you use to build, run, deploy, and manage Cloudflare Workers and everything attached to them.

item.title: Executor: one gateway to connect your AI agent to every tool
item.content:encoded: A look at Executor, an open-source, local-first layer that gives your AI agents one shared catalog of tools, with shared auth and built-in safety rules.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers: your first serverless function
item.content:encoded: What Cloudflare Workers are and how to build, run, and deploy your first one. The foundation of the whole Cloudflare developer platform.

item.title: Vercel eve: an open framework for building AI agents
item.content:encoded: A look at eve, Vercel's open-source agent framework. An agent is a directory of files, with durable execution, sandboxes, approvals, and evals built in.

item.title: Flue: the open framework for building AI agents
item.content:encoded: A guide to Flue, the open TypeScript framework for AI agents and workflows from Astro co-founder Fred Schott, covering agents, workflows and durability.

item.title: Val Town: write and deploy code in seconds
item.content:encoded: A hands-on tutorial for Val Town, where you write JavaScript and deploy it to a live URL instantly, with HTTP, cron, and email triggers plus SQLite storage.

item.title: A hands-on guide to The Agency, a collection of AI agents
item.content:encoded: How to install and use The Agency (agency-agents), a collection of specialized AI agents for Claude Code, Cursor, and other coding tools
